Context/Background:
Cancer-induced systemic inflammation is a dominant feature of cancer progression and metastatic spread. Clinically, systemic accumulation of myeloid cells is strongly correlated to poor prognosis in multiple solid malignancies, including breast cancer and a high neutrophil-to-lymphocyte (NLR) ratio is consistently associated with adverse outcomes. We, and others, previously published that primary tumors induce systemic accumulation and activation of neutrophils leading to enhanced metastatic spread in preclinical mouse models. In steady state, hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) give rise to all circulating blood cells through a series of progressively restrictive differentiation steps regulated by coordinated and temporal expression of transcription factors (TFs), leading to balanced bone marrow (BM) output. However, the molecular processes driving chronic, cancer-induced hematopoiesis, which leads to systemic inflammation, remain poorly understood.

We have previously demonstrated that expansion of metastasis-supporting neutrophils in mammary tumor-bearing K14cre;Cdh1fl/fl;Trp53fl/fl (KEP) mice is driven by an inflammatory cascade in which tumor associated macrophage (TAM)-derived IL-1β leads to elevated serum levels of G-CSF, the principal instructor of neutrophil generation. To understand how and at what stage of differentiation tumors drive neutrophil expansion, we clustered the genes upregulated in tumor-bearing mice based on their dynamics along the neutrophil pseudotime trajectory. We identified three groups of differentially expressed genes in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from KEP mice, which we termed early, middle, and late, based on their expression patterns. 

Early genes showed significant enrichment of an HSC-specific gene set. Upregulated early genes were overexpressed in HSCs and multipotent progenitors (MPPs) from KEP mice compared to cells from control mice but were repressed in cells that were further along the inferred neutrophil differentiation trajectory. Middle genes were defined as genes that were expressed around the transition from MPP to granulocyte monocyte progenitor (GMP). Lastly, upregulated/downregulated late genes, expressed in late GMP, granulocyte progenitor (GP), and pro-neutrophil (ProNeu) populations, were found to be expressed prematurely and at a higher level in progenitors from KEP mice.
Prompt: Provide a summary of the relevant pathways and genes that are up and down regulated in KEP vs WT mice in early, intermediate and late neutrophil development, focusing on how and at what stage of differentiation tumors drive neutrophil expansion.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Primary tumors in K14cre;Cdh1^fl/fl;Trp53^fl/fl (KEP) mammary carcinoma mice drive systemic neutrophil expansion via a TAM‐derived IL-1β→G-CSF axis, shifting HSC output toward the granulocyte lineage. To map where along the neutrophil differentiation trajectory this occurs, DE genes in KEP vs WT HSPCs were clustered by pseudotime into Early (HSC/MPP), Intermediate (MPP→GMP transition), and Late (late GMP→GP/ProNeu) modules, each showing “Up” or “Down” regulation in tumors. Only cluster membership was provided (no raw counts), so we performed ORA on each of the six gene lists to define pathway signatures at each stage. Details on sample sizes and raw fold-changes are not specified.  

Keywords  
• JAK–STAT signaling  
• Myc/metabolic rewiring  
• Unfolded protein/ER stress  
• Interleukin response  

Candidate Genes  
Il1r1, Stat3, Jak3, Cebpe, Shmt2, Phgdh  

1) Pathway Enrichments (ORA results)  
Up-Early (267 genes; MSigDB_Hallmark_2020, KEGG_2016, GO_BP_2023, Reactome_2024)  
Library: GO_Biological_Process_2023 (selected top terms)  
| Theme                                               | Direction | Leading Genes          | adj P-value  |  
|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------|------------------------|--------------|  
| Cellular Response To Interleukin-2 (GO:0071352)     | Up        | STAT3;IL2RG;JAK3       | 0.00515      |  
| Negative Regulation Of Receptor Signaling Via STAT  | Up        | SOCS1;SOCS3;BCL3;GBP7  | 0.00319      |  
Library: Reactome_Pathways_2024  
| Growth Hormone Receptor Signaling                   | Up        | GHR;SOCS1;SOCS2;CISH;STAT3;SOCS3 | 0.0000397 |  
| Signaling by Interleukins                            | Up        | IL1R1;PIK3CD;STAT3;JAK3;…           | 0.000120  |  

Down-Early (272 genes; same libraries)  
Library: GO_Biological_Process_2023  
| Regulation Of Rac Protein Signal Transduction        | Down      | ARHGAP17;OGT;PIK3CG;AUTS2 | 0.00910     |  
| Positive Regulation Of Filopodium Assembly           | Down      | FNBP1L;DOCK11;BCAS3;RIPOR2 | 0.03001     |  
Library: Reactome_Pathways_2024  
| Transcriptional Regulation by AP-2 (TFAP2) Family    | Down      | ESR1;APOE;KDM5B;KIT;KCTD1 | 0.00673     |  

Up-Intermediate (116 genes; MSigDB_Hallmark_2020, KEGG_2016)  
Library: MSigDB_Hallmark_2020  
| Myc Targets V1                                       | Up        | CAD;ODC1;SHMT2;BCAT1;TCP1;… | 0.0000417   |  
| G2-M Checkpoint                                      | Up        | NOLC1;NCL;E2F2;RPA2;…       | 0.000201    |  
Library: KEGG_2016  
| 2-Oxocarboxylic acid metabolism (hsa01210)           | Up        | GOT2;BCAT1                | 0.0780     |  

Down-Intermediate (123 genes; GO_Biological_Process_2023)  
| Positive Regulation Of Osteoclast Differentiation     | Down      | PPP3CA;TYROBP;NEDD9       | 0.0829     |  
| Cytoplasmic Sequestering Of NF-κB                   | Down      | NFKBIA;TMSB4X             | 0.1079     |  

Up-Late (266 genes; all four libraries)  
Library: Reactome_Pathways_2024  
| Metal Sequestration by Antimicrobial Proteins       | Up        | LCN2;S100A8;S100A9         | 0.00165    |  
Library: MSigDB_Hallmark_2020  
| mTORC1 Signaling                                    | Up        | LDHA;HSPA5;XBP1;…           | 9.6 × 10^-19 |  
Library: GO_Biological_Process_2023  
| Regulation Of ER Unfolded Protein Response         | Up        | HSPA5;XBP1;BAX             | 0.01244    |  
Library: KEGG_2016  
| Myc Targets V1 (via ORA fall-back)                  | Up        | LDHA;…                      | 1.47 × 10^-13 |  

Down-Late (98 genes; all libraries)  
Library: GO_Biological_Process_2023  
| Phospholipase C-activating Dopamine Receptor Signaling | Down   | GNA14;GNA15               | 0.0465     |  
Library: Reactome_Pathways_2024  
| Fatty Acids Bound to GPR40 Regulate Insulin Secretion | Down    | GNA14;GNA15               | 0.0427     |  
| Acetylcholine Regulates Insulin Secretion            | Down    | GNA14;GNA15               | 0.0475     |  

Analysis  
Early (HSC/MPP) Up genes are dominated by interleukin-family and JAK–STAT signaling (IL-2/7/9/15/21), implicating tumor-induced inflammatory priming of HSCs via IL-1β→IL-1R1→STAT3/JAK3. Down Early modules show suppression of Rho/Rac cytoskeletal and filopodial pathways, suggesting repressed motility signaling in non-granulocytic lineages. Intermediate (MPP→GMP) Up genes feature Myc-driven metabolic programs (one-carbon, amino-acid biosynthesis, G2-M checkpoint), indicating metabolic rewiring at the GMP transition. Down Intermediate genes reveal NF-κB sequestration and osteoclast differentiation modules, hinting at diversion from pro-neutrophil differentiation. Late (GMP→GP/ProNeu) Up genes exhibit ER stress/unfolded protein response and mTORC1 activation, reflecting high secretory and proliferation demands in proliferating ProNeu. Down Late clusters suppress GPCR-insulin–secretion pathways, consistent with lineage‐specific metabolic shifts.

2) Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtering Up-Early ORA for “Interleukin” terms confirmed enrichment of IL-2, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, IL-21 signaling (all adj P < 0.01) with leading edges STAT3, JAK3, IL2RG, SOCS1/3.  

3) Key Genes/Proteins (leading-edge)  
Up-regulated  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                  | Pathway(s)                                   |  
|--------|-----------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|  
| STAT3  | Up Early  | TF downstream of IL-1/G-CSF    | IL-2/7/9/15/21 signaling; JAK–STAT; IFN-γ     |  
| JAK3   | Up Early  | JAK family kinase              | IL-2/7/9/15 signaling; JAK–STAT               |  
| IL2RG  | Up Early  | Common γ-chain receptor subunit| IL-2/7/9/15 signaling                          |  
| SHMT2  | Up Int.   | Serine-glycine one-carbon enzyme| One-carbon metabolism; Myc targets            |  
| PHGDH  | Up Int.   | 3-Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase| Serine biosynthesis; Myc targets              |  

Down-regulated  
| Gene   | Direction     | Role/Function                  | Pathway(s)                                  |  
|--------|---------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|  
| CEBPE  | Down Int.     | Myeloid TF                      | Neutrophil granule gene activation          |  
| NFKBIA | Down Int.     | IκBα inhibitor of NF-κB         | NF-κB sequestration                          |  
| GNA14  | Down Late     | G protein subunit               | GPCR-insulin secretion                       |  

Comparisons  
• Early vs Intermediate: shift from immune-signaling (IL/JAK–STAT) to metabolic/Myc modules.  
• Intermediate vs Late: transition to stress-response (UPR, mTORC1) consistent with high anabolic/proliferative demands of ProNeu.  
• Down clusters at each stage feature suppression of alternative lineage programs (motility/B-cell, NF-κB, GPCR signaling).  

Implications  
Tumors co-opt early HSC/MPP via paracrine IL-1β/G-CSF to activate STAT3/JAK3, skewing differentiation toward GMP. Metabolic reprogramming at the GMP transition (via Myc and one-carbon) fuels expansion. Finally, proliferating late progenitors engage UPR and mTOR pathways to sustain high-output granulopoiesis. Therapeutically, targeting IL-1/STAT3 early or Myc-driven metabolism at the GMP stage may blunt neutrophil-driven metastasis.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate IL-1R1–STAT3 activation in KEP HSCs by phospho-STAT3 flow cytometry.  
2. Test small-molecule inhibitors of SHMT2/PHGDH in KEP mice to assess neutrophil output and metastatic burden.  
3. Examine UPR marker expression (XBP1 splicing; BiP) in late ProNeu.  
4. Check presence of classical cell-cycle signatures (E2F targets) in early clusters: ORA did not show E2F but G2/M checkpoint emerges in intermediate.  

References  
None (no PMIDs validated via literature-mining tools).
